programs.haiku:
"""Advance-planning words: the component fires on the words for "in advance" (reserve,
budget, expect, forecast, preview, preset), on the syllable right after a 預/预/予, and
weakly negative on the stem that follows a Russian verb prefix (под-, перед-, зад-, уд-,
объ-, прод-).

Heads, as single tokens: 預 and 预 (Chinese "pre-", as in 預約 reserve, 預算 budget),
予 (in advance), dự (Vietnamese "plan, forecast"), 예 (Korean "reserve, expect"), and the
English words "preview" and "preset". 余裕 fires on 裕 when it follows 余 ("margin").
Words where the head is merged into one token (预期, 预计, 预算, 预先, 预留, 预售, 预订,
预防) fire too. After 預/预/予 the next token fires as well (定 in 預定, 計 in 預計,
期 in 預期). Everything else predicts 0, except the Russian-prefix stems (-1).

Values are the typical activation of each case, read off the data. The carry holds the
previous token, cleared at a document boundary.
"""

READS = ()

HEAD = {
    "預": 10.0, "预": 9.0, "予": 5.0, "dự": 10.0, " dự": 10.0,
    "예": 4.0, " 예": 4.0,
    " preview": 4.4, " Preview": 5.4, "Preview": 2.5, " preset": 1.5,
}
WORD = {
    "预期": 5.0, "预计": 5.5, "预算": 4.0, "预先": 5.3, "预留": 4.2,
    "预售": 4.0, "预订": 4.8, "预防": 2.0,
}
AFTER_HEAD = {"預", "预", "予"}      # the next token after these fires (~4)
RUSSIAN_PREFIX = {" перед", " под", " Под", " зад", " уд", " объ", " прод"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev, prev_doc = carry if carry is not None else (None, None)
    if prev_doc != doc:
        prev = None
    new_carry = (cur, doc)
    if cur in HEAD:
        return new_carry, HEAD[cur]
    if cur in WORD:
        return new_carry, WORD[cur]
    if prev in AFTER_HEAD:
        return new_carry, 4.0
    if prev == "余" and cur == "裕":
        return new_carry, 8.5
    if prev in RUSSIAN_PREFIX:
        return new_carry, -1.0
    return new_carry, 0.0

"""Spelling detector for the letters 'cam' (and 'case'), as a word piece.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4673 is sparse and fires on a few specific
spellings in the current token:

- Strongly positive on the piece "cam" (also "Cam", "CAM", and pieces ending in
  "cam", e.g. "RICAM", "unicam"), roughly +5 to +10. Positive, smaller, on whole
  words "camera", "cameras", "camel", "cameroon" and "kam".
- Strongly negative on "case" right after "in" ("in case", "In case"), about -5
  to -7 in the data. Mildly negative on other "case" tokens, and on "cas", "cap",
  "cape", "casa", "caso", "casing", "aso", "ased" (about -1).
- Zero everywhere else. Predicting zero is the baseline the program beats.

Only the newest token and the one before it are read.
"""

READS = ()

CAM_WORDS = {"camera", "cameras", "camel", "cameroon", "kam"}
CAS_WORDS = {"cas", "cap", "cape", "casa", "caso", "casing", "aso", "ased"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if word.endswith("cam") and not word.startswith("s"):
        value = 5.5
    elif word in CAM_WORDS:
        value = 2.0
    elif word == "case":
        value = -5.0 if prev == "in" else -0.4
    elif word in CAS_WORDS:
        value = -0.8
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return None, value

programs.sol:
"""Coarse spelling and document-opening predictor.

The strongest observed event is an HTML declaration opener at a document's
first token. Otherwise, approximate a negative f/ph spelling bias (including
Greek phi, Cyrillic ef and Mandarin f initials). The Latin spelling bias is much stronger
at document starts, where capitalization and whitespace also matter.
It also recognizes a document-opening Title: heading and small markup
responses. Most lexical variation is left out.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
from pypinyin import lazy_pinyin

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def token_value(text, first):
    s = text.strip()
    low = s.lower().lstrip("._/([{\"'\\")
    han = bool(regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}', s))
    han_f = han and any(p.startswith('f') for p in lazy_pinyin(s))
    punctuation = bool(s) and not any(c.isalnum() for c in s)

    if first:
        value = 0.015
        value += 0.104 * text.startswith(' ')
        value -= 0.187 * s.isupper()
        value -= 0.079 * s.istitle()
        value -= 0.090 * s.islower()
        value += 0.055 * (s.isalpha() and len(s) > 6)
        value -= 0.145 * text.isspace()
        value -= 0.189 * s.isdecimal()
        value -= 0.078 * (han + punctuation)
        value -= 0.297 * ('f' in low)
        value -= 0.112 * low.startswith('f')
        value -= 0.263 * (low == 'f')
        value -= 0.257 * ('ph' in low)
        value -= 0.075 * ('ф' in low)
        value -= 0.137 * han_f
        value += 0.147 * s.startswith('<|')
    else:
        value = -0.003
        value -= 0.005 * ('f' in low)
        value -= 0.009 * low.startswith('f')
        value -= 0.057 * (low == 'f')
        value -= 0.024 * ('ph' in low)
        value -= 0.073 * ('ф' in low)
        value -= 0.097 * ('φ' in low or 'ϕ' in low)
        value -= 0.026 * han_f
        value += 0.151 * (bool(s) and set(s) == {'·'})
        value += 0.024 * (bool(s) and set(s) == {'_'})
        value += 0.041 * (s == '<')
        value -= 0.042 * (s == '{"')
        value += 0.012 * s.startswith('<|')
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = token_value(text, first)
    if first and text == '<!':
        value = 5.51
    elif not first and carry[1] and text == ':':
        value = 1.53  # Colon immediately after a document-opening 'Title'.
    return (doc, first and text == 'Title'), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj component 4674, as a word-and-document-start rule.

What the component is: a rank-one write into the residual stream whose main input is MLP
neuron 4674 of layer 1 (weight 0.38 on that neuron; the other neurons carry small weights).
That neuron is strongly negative on word-initial "f" tokens (fix, flex, fit, fin, fn, fact,
Frank, Ф...), and it is most extreme on the first token of a document, where attention
has no earlier context to look at (a row's first token, or the token after <|endoftext|>).

What this program predicts: a negative value on f-words, a more negative value on an
f-word that opens a document, a small negative value on any document opener, and 0 elsewhere.
It is a rule for the strongest, most readable part of the component, not all of it.
Most of the component's variance is small and spread over many neurons, and it is not
captured by word-level concepts, so this rule explains only about 1% of it.
"""

READS = ()

# Values the component takes on each case (nats of residual-stream write, in its own units).
F_WORD_OPENS_DOC = -0.44
OPENS_DOC = -0.05
F_WORD = -0.02


def _is_f_word(token):
    """Word-initial f (also ph, and Cyrillic ef, ф), ignoring a leading space and case."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    return word.startswith(("f", "ph", "ф"))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    opens_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    f_word = _is_f_word(prefix.token_strings[t])
    if opens_doc:
        value = F_WORD_OPENS_DOC if f_word else OPENS_DOC
    else:
        value = F_WORD if f_word else 0.0
    return None, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4675 -- a sparse feature on the second word of a technical compound.

What it does: it fires when the current word is the second half of a two-word
compound whose first word is a power / energy / resource / data / control /
memory / computing term, e.g. "power supply", "power management",
"resource usage", "energy efficiency", "data structure", "power plant".
Those tails get a clearly positive value (about 2). "device"/"devices" after
such a head gets a negative value (memory device, power devices), and bare
"device(s)" gets a small negative value. Everything else predicts 0.

It is a deliberately small, word-list program. It explains only the largest
spikes, and it misses most of the activation (see the explanation).
"""

READS = ()

HEAD_WORDS = {"power", "energy", "resource", "data", "control", "computational", "memory"}
POSITIVE_TAILS = {"usage", "consumption", "efficiency", "structure", "supply", "distribution",
                  "management", "unit", "plant", "play", "plays", "source", "cost", "board",
                  "allocation"}
NEGATIVE_TAILS = {"device", "devices", "gain", "intake", "value"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    head = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    if head in HEAD_WORDS:
        if word in POSITIVE_TAILS:
            return None, 2.0
        if word in NEGATIVE_TAILS:
            return None, -2.0
    if word in ("device", "devices"):
        return None, -0.4
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 4676: an "assistant role token" detector.

What it does: it fires strongly (about +0.9) on the word `assistant` when that word
is the role name right after a `<|im_start|>` chat-template marker, i.e. the start of
an assistant turn. Everywhere else it predicts 0.

Why: in the chat data this component's causal importance is ~1 only on those role
tokens. Switching the component off changes the model's next-token predictions very
little overall, so the component is a minor, role-specific signal.

Caveat: outside those tokens its real activation is a small, diffuse signal with no
simple token or character-class rule, so this program explains only a small share
of its variance (about 12%).
"""

READS = ()

ROLE_OPENER = "<|im_start|>"
ASSISTANT_ROLE = "assistant"
ASSISTANT_ACTIVATION = 0.91


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    if t >= 1 and strings[t] == ASSISTANT_ROLE and strings[t - 1] == ROLE_OPENER:
        return carry, ASSISTANT_ACTIVATION
    return carry, 0.0

"""Opening-quotation detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4677.

The component writes a positive signal onto the token that OPENS a quoted span
of text. It is strongest on a backslash-escaped quote inside a code string
(\\"), then on a quote that opens a value (="  {"  :"  ("), on opening curly
quotes, and on a quote that starts a quotation in prose. It is near zero on
closing quotes (", ” ' and \\", ) and on almost every other token.
"""

READS = ()

ESCAPED_OPEN = 1.0     # \" that starts a string in code or JSON
ESCAPED_CLOSE = 0.2    # \" followed by ) or , : closing the string
HEREDOC = 1.5          # the EOF in  <<'EOF'
VALUE_OPEN = 0.4       # " right after = { : ( (opens a value or argument)
PROSE_OPEN = 0.4       # " starting a quotation after a space, sentence end or line start
WORD_QUOTE = 0.1       # " right after a word: usually a closing quote
CURLY_OPEN = 0.5       # “ „ « ‘ 「 『
CURLY_CHARS = set("“„«‘「『")
VALUE_BEFORE = set("={:(")


def quote_value(prev, tok):
    body = tok.lstrip(" ")
    if "\\\"" in tok:
        closing = '\\")' in tok or '\\",' in tok
        return ESCAPED_CLOSE if closing else ESCAPED_OPEN
    if body[:1] in CURLY_CHARS:
        return CURLY_OPEN
    if '"' not in body:
        return 0.0
    before = tok[: tok.index('"')]
    if before[-1:] in VALUE_BEFORE:
        return VALUE_OPEN
    if not prev or prev[-1:] in " \n\t.([":
        return PROSE_OPEN
    if prev[-1:].isalnum():
        return WORD_QUOTE
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    if tok == "EOF" and "<<" in prev:
        return carry, HEREDOC
    return carry, quote_value(prev, tok)

"""Import-directive keywords in semicolon-terminated code (Java, C#, PHP, Rust, C++).

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4679 is silent almost everywhere (typical values are
within about 1 of zero) and spikes negative on the keyword that opens an import-style
directive line, when the line before it is itself a semicolon-ended directive:

  package com.example.app;      <- directive line
  (blank line)
  import java.util.List;        <- "import" here: about -25 (largest)

The same holds for `use` and `using` (PHP, Rust, C#): about -10 after a `...;` directive.
In line-numbered code listings (`    21<TAB>import ...`) the tab-indented keyword is
about -11. A Java stack-trace line (`<TAB>at pkg.Class.method(File.java:30)`) gives about
-10 on its `at`.

Not active: Python's `import x` (after a newline, not a `;`), JavaScript's
`import x from 'y';` (the `from` marks it as JS), and a document's first keyword.

The program keeps the last non-empty line before the current token, drops any leading
line number, and fires on the keyword only in these cases.
"""

READS = ()

# Lines that open a directive in a compiled or semicolon-based language.
DIRECTIVE_STARTS = ("import ", "package ", "using ", "use ", "namespace ")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    raw = prefix.token_strings[t]  # the token alone, e.g. "import" or "\timport"
    word = raw.strip()
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t - 1] != prefix.document_ids[t]:
        return None, 0.0

    # Text of the last ~80 tokens, with <|endoftext|> and literal "\n" read as newlines.
    recent = "".join(prefix.token_strings[max(0, t - 80) : t])
    recent = recent.replace("<|endoftext|>", "\n").replace("\\n", "\n")
    lines = [x.strip() for x in recent.split("\n") if x.strip()]
    prev = lines[-1].lstrip("0123456789 \t") if lines else ""  # drop a leading line number

    after_directive = (
        prev.startswith(DIRECTIVE_STARTS) and prev.endswith(";") and " from " not in prev
    )
    if word in ("import", "use", "using") and after_directive:
        if word == "import" and raw.startswith("\t"):
            return None, -11.0  # indented import in a numbered listing
        return None, (-25.0 if word == "import" else -10.0)

    # Java stack trace: "\tat pkg.Class.method(File.java:30)" after a line ending in ")".
    if raw == "\tat" and lines and lines[-1].endswith(")"):
        return None, -10.0
    return None, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Recognize a small spelling neighbourhood around 'shell' and 'shed'.

Whole-token and token-split spellings have different strengths. In particular,
sh + ell/ed is positive, whereas sh + ui/ri/ov is negative. Most other text
is zero. Parallel Cyrillic and Hebrew spellings, Chinese shell characters,
repeated middle dots and an initial Title: label have separate small rules.
Only the newest token and a short suffix of its document are used.
"""
import re
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()

# Whole-token spellings, not arbitrary occurrences inside longer words.
WORDS = (
    (r'shells?', 4.8),
    (r'powershell', 6.5),
    (r'shed|sheds|shedding', 3.4),
    (r'shelley', 3.2),
    (r'shel', 2.0),
    (r'shelf|shelves|shaw|shores?', 1.1),
    (r'shard', 2.2),
    (r'shark|sheldon|ashley', 0.8),
    (r'shim', -4.5),
    (r'shan|shame|shale|schul', -2.2),
    (r'shave|shaved|shaving', -2.5),
    (r'shi|shin|shah|sharon|shen|shawn|shane|shaun|sho', -1.0),
    (r'sh|sha', -0.35),
)
WORDS = tuple((re.compile(p), v) for p, v in WORDS)

# Endings that complete a spelling across a token boundary after sh/sch.
ENDINGS = (
    (r'ell|ells|elled', 7.0),
    (r'el', 4.8),
    (r'ed', 5.8),
    (r'ards?', 4.9),
    (r'ark', 2.6),
    (r'ore|ores|awl|aw|eng|erd|erry|err|atter|attering', 1.9),
    (r'ock|opping|oppers|ady|aded|ields|reds', 1.0),
    (r'ui', -9.0),
    (r'oving|oves|ov|out', -5.0),
    (r'ri|aved|aving|avers', -3.7),
    (r'u|uang|uhan|ua|uai|uib|an|me|ims|ivers|osh', -2.7),
    (r'in|im|ah|ahr|ane|am|f|r|re|ul|uh|udd', -1.5),
    (r'annon|ag', 0.5),
)
ENDINGS = tuple((re.compile(p), v) for p, v in ENDINGS)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    raw, age = (b'', 0) if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1:]
    newest = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    text = newest.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    previous = raw.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    word = text.strip(' \t\r\n-_').lower()
    value = 0.0
    for pattern, strength in WORDS:
        if pattern.fullmatch(word):
            value = strength
            break
    if word == 'shell' and not text[:1].isspace():
        value = 6.5 if text.startswith(('-', '_')) else 7.0
    # Preserve word boundaries: whitespace must never join two spellings.
    if previous and previous[-1].isalpha() and text[:1].isalpha():
        tail = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+\Z', previous)
        tail = tail.group().lower() if tail else ''
        if tail.endswith(('sh', 'sch')):
            for pattern, strength in ENDINGS:
                if pattern.fullmatch(text.lower()):
                    # -ed after 'brush' is an ordinary suffix, not 'shed'.
                    bare = tail in ('sh', 'sch')
                    if text.lower() in ('ed', 'out') and not bare:
                        break
                    value = strength * (1.0 if bare else 0.8)
                    break
            if text.lower() in ('ley', 'leigh', 'able'):
                value = 4.3 if text.lower() != 'able' else 1.6
        if tail.endswith('s') and text.lower() == 'hell':
            value = 6.5
        if tail in ('she',) and text.lower() in ('ath', 'aths', 'athing'):
            value = 5.5 if text.lower() != 'athing' else 2.9
        # Similar sh + e/l spellings in Cyrillic and related alphabets.
        if previous.lower().endswith(('ш', 'щ', 'š')):
            ending = anyascii(text).lower()
            if ending in ('el', 'ed', 'estv'):
                value = 4.5
            elif ending in ('l', 'lo', 'li', 'la'):
                value = 2.8
    joined = (raw + newest).decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    # Shin followed by the Hebrew sheva vowel sign, including split UTF-8.
    if joined.endswith('שְ') and not previous.endswith('שְ'):
        value = 5.8
    elif (raw + newest).endswith('ש'.encode() + b'\xd6'):
        value = 2.5
    if word in ('壳', '殼'):
        value = 2.8
    if text == '··' and previous.endswith('··'):
        value = -1.85
    if text == ':' and previous == 'Title' and age == 1:
        value = -4.73
    return (doc, (raw + newest)[-48:], age + 1), value
programs.haiku:
"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 4680: a "shell / shed / shard" word detector.

The component writes into the residual stream when the text being read spells one of a few
English words that begin "sh" and end in "-ell", "-ed", "-ard", "-eath" or "-elf", such as
"shell", "shed", "shard", "sheath", and the nearby "shelf", "shelves", "shore", "shark".
It responds to the letters that finish the word, however they are split into tokens:
" shell" or "shell" as one token, "sh" + "ell", "sh" + "ard" (ShardDoc), "Sh" + "ed" +
"ding". Its value is set by the word typed so far (lower case). It is strongest on the
piece that completes the word and near zero on the earlier "sh" piece. Other "sh" words
(should, show, shop, sheet, shut, shelter) predict 0.

The values are the average activations on a training sample for each word. Everything
else predicts 0.

What this simple version gets: about 11% of the variance on eval rows (r = 0.34), and it
nearly matches switching the component off in the model (kl_fraction 0.86). A table with
one value per token would reach about 0.2 on held-out sample rows, and about 0.48 in-sample,
but most of the extra comes from many small, diffuse values (about 0.1 to 0.5) on ordinary
subword pieces that share no concept.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Typical activation when the word typed so far (lower case) is this word.
WORD_VALUES = {
    "shell": 5.3, "shells": 4.5, "shelled": 5.4, "shelling": 5.4,
    "shed": 3.6, "sheds": 2.5, "shedding": 3.9,
    "shard": 3.7, "sheath": 6.0, "sheathing": 2.9,
    "shel": 2.0, "shelf": 0.9, "shelves": 1.2,
    "shore": 1.1, "shores": 1.3, "ashore": 2.3, "shark": 1.2,
}


def word_so_far(prefix):
    """Letters of the word that ends at the newest token, within its document."""
    word = ""
    newest_doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    for i in range(len(prefix.token_strings) - 1, -1, -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != newest_doc:
            break
        piece = prefix.token_strings[i]
        letters = re.search(r"[^\W\d_]*$", piece).group(0)
        word = letters + word
        if letters != piece:
            break
    return word.lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token: the value of the word typed so far, else 0."""
    return None, float(WORD_VALUES.get(word_so_far(prefix), 0.0))

"""Negative activation at three kinds of position, zero elsewhere.

1. The token that opens a declaration's body. A C-like, Go, Rust, JS, Java or C# header
   line (function, method, class or struct: keywords such as func, fn, function, void, int,
   public, class) ends at a '{'; that brace gets a negative value. A Python def or class
   line ends at the ':' outside its parentheses; that colon gets a negative value.
   Control-flow lines (if, for, while, ...), assignments and object literals do not count.
2. The first token of each document: a row's first token, or the first token after a
   document change, has no preceding text in its document, so it gets a negative value.
3. A run of dot leaders, the token '··' (two middle dots): strongly negative.
"""
import re

READS = ()

CONTROL = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(if|for|while|switch|catch|else|elif|with|return|do|try|case|foreach|using|new|throw|yield|await)\b"
)
DECLARATION = re.compile(
    r"\b(def|func|fn|function|class|struct|interface|enum|impl|type|namespace|void|int|bool|char|"
    r"double|float|String|string|public|private|protected|static|async|export|override|package)\b"
)
PY_HEADER = re.compile(r"^\s*(async\s+)?(def|class)\b")
BRACE_VALUE = -0.8
PY_COLON_VALUE = -0.5
DOC_START_VALUE = -0.28
DOT_RUN_VALUE = -1.15


def opener_value(line, mark):
    """Value of a '{' or ':' that ends `line`, if it opens a declaration body; else 0."""
    if CONTROL.match(line) or "=" in line:
        return 0.0
    if mark == "{":
        return BRACE_VALUE if DECLARATION.search(line) else 0.0
    # A ':' counts only as the end of a Python def or class header, outside parentheses.
    depth = line.count("(") - line.count(")") + line.count("[") - line.count("]")
    if PY_HEADER.match(line) and depth == 0:
        return PY_COLON_VALUE
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the text of the current line so far, and of the last non-blank line before it.
    cur, prev = carry if carry is not None else ("", "")
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        cur, prev = "", ""
        value = DOC_START_VALUE
    elif tok.count("·") >= 2 and not tok.strip("· "):
        value = DOT_RUN_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
        for i, ch in enumerate(tok):
            if ch in "{:" and not tok[i:].startswith("://"):

introduce a clause or describe a manner, in these languages:

    'ท' about -4.4, and the second half 'ี่' after 'ท' about -9.8
  - Thai 'อัน' (a prenominal "which"): about -7 on its last part
  - Thai 'ซึ่ง' (which): about -2 on its last part
  - Thai 'อย่าง' ("in a way / such as"): about -6 on its last part
  - Swedish/Norwegian 'som' ("who/which/as"): about -3.3
  - Scandinavian 'det' (it/that): about -2.4; capitalised 'Det' about -3.4
  - Greek 'που' (that/which): about -5.5 on its last part
  - English 'which', German 'der' and 'den' (articles and most uses): about 0
A repeated middle-dot filler '··' sits at a steady +0.86.
Everything else predicts 0. Values are typical activations (not fitted per token)."""

    " التي": -6.3, " الذي": -6.3, " الذين": -6.3, " والتي": -6.3, " التى": -6.3, " الذى": -6.3, "ذي": -6.3,
    "ท": -4.4,

    if tok == "ี่" and prev == "ท":

"""Layer 1, MLP down_proj, component 4689: the syllable "ao" inside names and split words,
plus a small negative value on the first token of each document.

The component is nearly silent almost everywhere. Two things move it:

1. It fires on a token whose text is the syllable "ao" or "ão" as a piece of a name
   or split word: "Sao" (Sao Paulo, Sao Tome), "Yao", "Tao", "Zhao", "iao", "Dao",
   "Joao", "AO", and "ao" pieces inside romanised Chinese names ("Xia|oy|u") or code
   identifiers ("ao1"). Common Portuguese words (não, são, ...) and words with ç
   ("ação", "ção") do not fire. A lowercase "ao" that opens a new word (Portuguese
   "ao" = "to the") is weak.

2. The first token of a document (the row's start, or a token after <|endoftext|>)
   sits slightly below zero, on average -0.19.

  capitalised or uppercase piece                   3.3
  lowercase piece attached to the word before it   3.7
  lowercase piece after a space (a new word)       0.4
and a document's first token gets -0.2.
"""

READS = ()

# Common Portuguese words ending in "ao"/"ão" that are not name pieces.
COMMON_WORDS = {"não", "são", "mão", "pão", "vão", "ão"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        return carry, -0.2
    word = text.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    if not lower.endswith(("ao", "ão")) or "ç" in lower or lower in COMMON_WORDS:
        return carry, 0.0
    if word[:1].isupper():
        value = 3.3
    elif text.startswith(" "):
        value = 0.4
    else:

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 4690: a document-opener detector.

In plain terms: this component is silent inside a document, and only speaks at the first
token of each document, where the model has no context yet. There its value depends on what
that token looks like: rare non-Latin scripts (Hangul, Katakana, Thai, Hiragana, Arabic,
Cyrillic, Han) give large positive values, a capitalised Latin word opener a small positive
one, and lowercase or space-led fragments and ASCII digits about zero or slightly positive.
Two tokens are fixed: a document that opens with `import` (a Python file), and the middle-dot
run '··' (a degenerate repetition that gives a constant large value wherever it occurs).

Where a document starts is read from `document_ids` (a change of label resets the count),
exactly as the model resets its attention and positions.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

# Mean activation at a document's first token, by what the token looks like.
OPENER = {
    "HANGUL": 22.8,
    "KATAKANA": 5.4,
    "THAI": 4.6,
    "HIRAGANA": 2.1,
    "ARABIC": 1.5,
    "CYRILLIC": 1.2,
    "CJK": 0.9,
    "special": 1.9,
    "Latin-capital": 0.8,
    "Latin-lowercase": 0.5,
    "Latin-spaced": 0.2,
    "punctuation": 0.2,
    "other": 0.2,
    "digit": -0.1,
    "space": 0.0,
}

SCRIPTS = ("HANGUL", "KATAKANA", "HIRAGANA", "THAI", "ARABIC", "CYRILLIC", "CJK")


def kind(token):
    """The class of a token's first visible character."""
    if token.startswith("<|"):
        return "special"
    visible = [c for c in token if not c.isspace()]
    if not visible:
        return "space"
    c = visible[0]
    name = unicodedata.name(c, "")
    for script in SCRIPTS:
        if script in name:
            return script
    if c.isascii() and c.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if c.isascii() and c.isalpha():
        if token[0] == " ":
            return "Latin-spaced"
        return "Latin-capital" if c.isupper() else "Latin-lowercase"
    if c.isascii():
        return "punctuation"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == "··":
        return None, 7.8
    first = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not first:
        return None, 0.0
    if token == "import":
        return None, 7.4
    return None, OPENER[kind(token)]

"""Document-start detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4691.

This component is almost silent except on the first token of a document. On a document's
first token it goes negative, about -0.15 on average (the mean over training positions
with that property, with a spread of about 0.3 around it depending on the token). Everywhere
else it is near zero, with small noise of about 0.04.

The program says: a document starts here, so predict the typical value -0.15; otherwise 0.
A row packs several documents end to end, and a new document begins at row position 0 or
wherever the document id changes, so both count as starts. Each position is judged from
its own prefix only, so the program is causal, and it keeps no state between positions.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START_VALUE = -0.15


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, (DOC_START_VALUE if starts_document else 0.0)

"""Approximate negative peaks on scrambled letters and biological notation.

Keep a 32-token summary of short, unspaced ASCII fragments. Their negative
response grows with density and a small, varied character alphabet. Also
recognize diverse DNA/RNA base strings and amino-acid abbreviation prefixes
after two distinct residues. These classes cover large training peaks;
token-specific magnitudes are deliberately not modeled. Chat role and
reasoning/tool delimiter offsets are handled separately. Reset per document.
"""
from collections import Counter, deque

READS = ()
BASES = frozenset('ACGTUN')
AMINO_ACIDS = frozenset('''
Ala Arg Asn Asp Cys Gln Glu Gly His Ile
Leu Lys Met Phe Pro Ser Thr Trp Tyr Val
'''.split())
AMINO_PREFIXES = {a[:n] for a in AMINO_ACIDS for n in (1, 2, 3)}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', (deque(), Counter(), 0, 0), ('', 0, frozenset()))
    _, previous, shape, spelling = carry
    history, alphabet, short_count, letter_count = shape
    word, pieces, amino_seen = spelling

    # Summarize recent character fragments.
    plain = s.isascii() and s.isalnum()
    short = plain and len(s) <= 3
    letters = short and any(c.isalpha() for c in s)
    chars = set(c for c in s if c.isascii() and c.isalnum())
    history.append((short, letters, chars))
    short_count += short
    letter_count += letters
    alphabet.update(chars)
    if len(history) > 32:
        old_short, old_letters, old_chars = history.popleft()
        short_count -= old_short
        letter_count -= old_letters
        for c in old_chars:
            alphabet[c] -= 1
            if not alphabet[c]:
                del alphabet[c]

    fragments = bases = amino_start = amino_end = 0.0
    if plain and sum(c.isalpha() for c in alphabet) >= 4:
        density = max(0.0, short_count / 32 - 0.6)
        letter_fraction = letter_count / max(1, short_count)
        fragments = density * letter_fraction / max(8, len(alphabet) + 1)

    # Follow the current word and possible biological sequences.
    raw = s.lstrip(' ')
    if raw and raw.isascii() and raw.isalpha():
        if s.startswith(' '):
            word, pieces = '', 0
        word_start = not word
        word += raw
        pieces += 1
        if word in AMINO_PREFIXES:
            if len(amino_seen) >= 2:
                if word_start:
                    amino_start = len(raw) / 3
                else:
                    amino_end = len(raw) / 3
            if word in AMINO_ACIDS:
                amino_seen = amino_seen | {word}
        else:
            amino_seen = frozenset()
        alphabetic_bases = set(word.upper())
        if (len(word) >= 5 and pieces >= 3 and alphabetic_bases <= BASES
                and len(alphabetic_bases - {'N'}) >= 3):
            bases = min(3, pieces - 2)
    else:
        word, pieces = '', 0
        if not s.isspace():
            amino_seen = frozenset()

    value = -0.002 - 138 * fragments - 1.5 * bases
    value -= 5.2 * amino_start + 1.0 * amino_end
    # Explicit chat markup overrides the text-shape response.
    if previous == '<|im_start|>':
        value = {'user': 0.55, 'system': 0.20, 'assistant': -0.045}.get(s, value)
    elif s in ('<tool_call>', '<tool_response>', '<think>'):
        value = 0.30
    elif s == '</think>':
        value = 0.096
    elif s in ('</tool_call>', '</tool_response>'):
        value = -0.07
    elif s == '<|im_start|>':
        value = 0.173 if previous in ('', '<|endoftext|>') else 0.005

    carry = (doc, s, (history, alphabet, short_count, letter_count),
             (word, pieces, amino_seen))
    return carry, max(-7.0, float(value))

"""Layer-1 MLP component 4692 (down_proj): random-text detector plus chat and filler markup.

What it does
- Negative on random-looking, encoded or machine-scrambled text: base64 blobs,
  hashes, ciphertext, letter soup such as "neimocny neioycmn ...". Scrambled
  letter strings give the largest negatives (down to about -9 in training data);
  base64 and hash-like strings give around -0.5 to -1 at this scale.
- Positive on chat and tool markup: the role word "user" right after
  "<|im_start|>" (about +0.56), "<tool_response>" and "<tool_call>" (about +0.3),
  and "<think>" (about +0.28).
- Positive (+1.4) on runs of middle dots, the filler "········".
- Ordinary English, code and punctuation predict 0.

Why the random-text rule works: a BPE tokenizer chops random text into many tiny
glued pieces, while ordinary prose uses longer tokens and spaces. So the program
counts how many of the last WINDOW tokens (same document only) are short
letters-only fragments (1-3 ASCII letters, no leading space). When that density
is high, the current token (if it is a letter or digit) gets a negative value
that grows with it.
"""

READS = ()

WINDOW = 24     # recent tokens looked back over, within the same document
FLOOR = 0.4     # fragment density below which the random-text rule predicts 0
SCALE = 0.6     # activation at full fragment density
MARKUP = {"<tool_response>": 0.32, "<tool_call>": 0.30, "<think>": 0.28}
DOT_FILLER = 1.4  # runs of middle dots, as in "········"
USER_TURN = 0.56


def _fragment(text):
    """A short piece of a word: 1-3 ASCII letters, no leading space."""
    return 0 < len(text) <= 3 and text.isascii() and text.isalpha()


def _alnum(text):
    return len(text) > 0 and text.isascii() and text.isalnum()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    texts = prefix.token_strings
    if texts[t] == "user" and t > 0 and texts[t - 1] == "<|im_start|>":
        return carry, USER_TURN
    if texts[t] in MARKUP:
        return carry, MARKUP[texts[t]]
    if texts[t] and set(texts[t]) == {"\u00b7"}:
        return carry, DOT_FILLER
    start = max(0, t - WINDOW + 1)
    fragments = sum(
        1 for i in range(start, t + 1) if docs[i] == docs[t] and _fragment(texts[i])
    )
    density = fragments / WINDOW
    if not _alnum(texts[t]) or density <= FLOOR:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, -SCALE * min(1.0, (density - FLOOR) / (1 - FLOOR))

A few completion labels, copyright wording, Japanese comparisons and the
quarter sign have lexical responses too. All other tokens predict zero.

import re

# Endings, matching opening prepositions, unpaired and paired strengths.
PHRASES = [
    ('下 下的', '在', .3, -4.2),
    ('之下 底下', '在', -.4, -2.2),
    ('中 中的', '在', -.2, -1.3),
    ('之中 当中 當中', '在', -.45, -1.1),
    ('内 內 里 裡 内的 內的 里的 裡的', '在', -.05, -1.0),
    ('范围内 範圍內 之内 之內 短时间内 短時間內', '在', -.2, -1.0),
    ('上 上的 之上', '在', .02, -.18),
    ('来说 來說 而言', '对對', -1.2, -4.0),
    ('看来 看來', '在', -.15, -3.2),
    ('相比', '与與和跟比', -1.2, -4.8),
    ('一样 一樣 那样 那樣 样 樣 样的 樣的', '和跟与與比像如', -.27, -2.1),
    ('不同 相同', '与與和跟比', -.08, -1.0),
    ('一起 一同 一起来 一起來', '与與和跟', -.9, -3.5),
    ('共同 合作 相结合 相結合 相连 相連 无关 無關', '与與和跟', -.09, -1.0),
    ('出发 出發', '从從', 0., -1.4),

    ('より', '', -.25, -.25),

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    past, previous = ('', '') if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1:]

    # Abstract support and circumstances, even when the opening 在 is omitted.
    if s in {'下', '下的'}:

                            '建议', '建議', '推动', '推動', '驱动', '驅動')):

"""Chinese frame-closing words.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4693 is a "frame closer" detector for Chinese. It goes
negative on the word that ends a frame opened a few characters earlier:
  在X下 / 在X的情况下 ("under X"), 在X中 ("in X"), 对于X来说 ("as for X"),
  与X相比 ("compared with X"), 在X看来 ("in X's view"), 对X而言 ("for X"),
  与X一起 ("together with X"), 与X一样 ("the same as X").
The closing word is what the component responds to. The frame's opener (在 for 下/中/里,
对于/与/对 for 来说/相比/而言/看来/一起/一样) must appear within the last WINDOW characters of
the same document; without one the same word is near zero. The English word "possible"
(as in "the possible solutions") gives a small positive value.

The predicted value is a typical activation for that closer, rounded from about 2 million
training tokens. Closer words not listed predict 0.
"""

READS = ()

WINDOW = 20
ZAI = ("在",)                                   # opener of 在X下 / 在X中 frames
OTHER = ("对于", "与", "和", "跟", "从", "按照", "根据", "对")

# closing word -> (value with 在 in the window, value with another opener in the window)
CLOSERS = {
    "下": (-3.3, -0.7),
    "之下": (-2.0, -1.0),
    "情况下": (-2.1, -2.0),
    "的情况下": (-1.5, -1.5),
    "中": (-1.2, -0.3),
    "之中": (-1.1, -0.5),
    "里": (-0.9, -0.2),
    "内": (-0.5, -0.2),
    "內": (-1.0, -0.4),
    "来说": (-3.5, -3.7),
    "相比": (-4.9, -4.9),
    "看来": (-3.5, -3.5),
    "而言": (-4.0, -4.0),
    "一起": (-2.7, -2.7),
    "一样": (-1.5, -1.5),
    "一樣": (-2.7, -2.7),
    "基础上": (-1.6, -1.6),
    "过程中": (-0.6, -0.6),
}

POSITIVE = {" possible": 0.4}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (recent text in this document, document id of the last token)
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    recent = carry[0] if carry is not None and carry[1] == doc else ""
    value = 0.0
    if tok in CLOSERS:
        zai_value, other_value = CLOSERS[tok]
        if any(z in recent for z in ZAI):
            value = zai_value
        elif any(o in recent for o in OTHER):
            value = other_value
    elif tok in POSITIVE:
        value = POSITIVE[tok]
    recent = (recent + tok)[-WINDOW:]
    return (recent, doc), value

The component fires on the dot-suffix token that closes a website name, such as
".com" in "github.com", ".org" in "en.wikipedia.org" or ".io" in "candybox2.github.io"
(also e-mail hosts like "name@mit.edu"). It is silent on file extensions (".py", ".json",
".md"), on code members (".append", ".get"), and on Java package paths such as
"import br.com.zup", where "com" is not a domain.

Prediction: a known top-level domain token, right after a word, on a line that is not an
import/package line. Strong for the common generic and academic suffixes (.org, .net, .edu,
.gov, .io, .uk), medium for the rest (.com, country codes). Zero everywhere else.
"""

READS = ()

TLDS = {
    "com", "org", "net", "edu", "gov", "io", "info", "biz", "xyz", "app", "dev",
    "uk", "de", "pl", "ch", "au", "fr", "be", "co", "ca", "ru", "jp", "cn", "tw",
    "kr", "us", "in", "ai", "ua", "se", "dk", "tv", "me",
}
STRONG = {"org", "net", "edu", "gov", "io", "uk"}
STRONG_VALUE = 9.0
WEAK_VALUE = 5.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if not (cur.startswith(".") and cur[1:] in TLDS):
        return None, 0.0
    # a domain name word must come right before the dot-suffix
    if len(prefix) < 2 or not prefix.token_strings[-2][-1:].isalnum():
        return None, 0.0

    line = ""
    for s in reversed(prefix.token_strings[:-1]):
        if "\n" in s:
            line = s.split("\n")[-1] + line

    return None, STRONG_VALUE if cur[1:] in STRONG else WEAK_VALUE

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4696 - a document-opening component.

Its large values are at the first two tokens of a document (a document starts after
<|endoftext|>, and at the start of each packed row); those two positions carry about a fifth
of its variance. Deeper inside a document it is small and token-specific (the same token
gives the same small value), and no short concept captures that, so this program predicts 0
there.

At a document's first token it reads what kind of token opens the text:
  - a capitalised word (a sentence opener such as "The", "Person")   -> positive
  - a lowercase word                                                 -> slightly positive
  - a digit                                                          -> negative
  - a special token or other punctuation                             -> about zero
At the document's second token, digits are the main story: the opening "1 2" (a document
beginning "12") drives it strongly negative, and a repeated digit ("11", "22", "00") is
mildly negative.
Everything else predicts 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

START_CAPITAL = 0.19
START_LOWER = 0.07
START_DIGIT = -0.16
START_SPECIAL = -0.07
TWO_ONE_TWO = -3.16      # "1" then "2" as the first two tokens of a document
REPEATED_DIGIT = -0.25   # the same digit twice as the first two tokens


def _start_value(s):
    word = s.strip()
    if not word:
        return 0.0
    if word.startswith("<|"):
        return START_SPECIAL
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+", word):
        return START_DIGIT
    if word[0].isupper():
        return START_CAPITAL
    if word[0].isalpha():
        return START_LOWER
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (tokens so far in this document, the document's first token string)
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        return (1, s), _start_value(s)
    n, first = carry
    value = 0.0
    if n == 1:
        if first == "1" and s == "2":
            value = TWO_ONE_TWO
        elif first == s and s.isdigit():
            value = REPEATED_DIGIT
    return (n + 1, first), value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4697: a rule-based sketch.

The component is almost silent on most tokens. Its clearest behaviour is negative:

  1. The first token of each document. Nothing precedes it, so the activation depends
     on the token alone: about -0.26 on average.
  2. A run of layout spaces inside a line, not right after a line break: table or
     column padding, or wide gaps in wrapped text. The longer the run, the more
     negative: about -0.015 per space, so -0.1 at 7 spaces and -0.3 at 20.
  3. A row of middle dots used as a dotted leader ("········"): about -0.57.

Everything else is predicted as 0. Most of the component's variance is spread thinly
over ordinary tokens with no shared concept, so this program explains only a small
share of it; the rules above carry the large and clearly structured values.
"""

READS = ()

DOT = "·"
DOCUMENT_START = -0.26
DOT_LEADER = -0.57
SPACE_PER_CHAR = -0.015
MIN_SPACE_RUN = 5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, DOCUMENT_START
    if tok and set(tok) == {DOT}:
        return carry, DOT_LEADER
    if len(tok) >= MIN_SPACE_RUN and set(tok) == {" "}:
        if "\n" not in prefix.token_strings[-2]:
            return carry, SPACE_PER_CHAR * len(tok)
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 4698: a spelling detector for "aware".

It is lexical. It reads the word being spelled out, i.e. the letters since the last
non-letter character, joining subword tokens (so "A" + "ware" is the word "aware").

- "aware", "awareness", "unaware", "Aware...": strongly active, about 5.
- "warehouse" (and Chinese 仓 / 仓库, warehouse): about 5.
- other words ending in "ware" (oneware, homeware, ware): about 1.6. Not
  software, hardware, firmware, middleware, vmware, which stay at 0.
- German "wahr" pieces (wahr, Wahrzeichen, Wahrheit): about 1.5.
- "wise", "-wise", "wan", "wart", "wage", "wager": about 1.
- The first token of a document that starts partway through a packed row: -0.2.
- Anything else: 0.

Main logic: the value depends only on the current word. The word-so-far is carried
forward token by token and reset at each document start.
"""

import re

READS = ()

STRONG = ("aware", "warehouse", "仓", "仓库")
NOT_WARE = ("software", "hardware", "firmware", "middleware", "vmware")
MILD = ("wan", "wart", "wage", "wager", "wah", "wis")


def value_of(word, token):
    if any(s in word for s in STRONG) or token.strip() in STRONG:
        return 5.0
    if word.endswith("ware") and word not in NOT_WARE:
        return 1.6
    if word.startswith("wah") or word.endswith("wahr"):
        return 1.5
    if word.endswith("wise") or word in MILD:
        return 1.0
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc_start = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    word = "" if doc_start else carry
    # Letters of this token after its last non-letter character.
    tail = re.split(r"[^A-Za-z]", token)[-1].lower()
    if re.search(r"[^A-Za-z]", token):
        word = tail
    else:
        word = word + tail
    value = value_of(word, token)
    if value == 0 and doc_start and prefix.position > 0:
        value = -0.2  # a document starting partway through a packed row
    return word, value

"""Layer 1, MLP down_proj, component 4699: a "before" detector.

What it does: it fires on words that mean "before" (earlier in time, or in front of), in
several languages, and on the words that set up a "before" phrase.
  * Before-words: "before", "avant" (French), "antes" (Spanish), "bevor" / "vor" (German),
    "voor" (Dutch), "ante", "prima" (Italian), "davanti" / "devant", "قبل", "trước".
    English "before" is weaker in "as before" (= as previously).
  * Words split across tokens, when the joined pieces spell a before-word: "V"+"or" (Vor-),
    "Av"+"ant" (avant), "Ant"+"es" (antes), "be"+"fore", "v"+"oor".
  * "of" completing "in front of", "ahead of", "in advance of", "eve of": the strongest
    response, about 10.
  * "to" after "prior" ("prior to"), about 4; "for" after "ready", "prepared",
    "preparation" ("ready for"), about 3; "of" after "anticipation" (about 3); "front" and
    "advance" after "in", about 4.5. A bare "vor" or "voor" inside a word, about 3.
Everything else predicts 0. The numbers are typical activations on training text.

Why: the component carries "something comes before / in front of" into the residual
stream. A word list plus a few context rules captures most of its variance.
"""

READS = ()

# Words meaning "before", with their typical activation.
BEFORE = {
    "before": 2.9, "vor": 6.0, "voor": 6.0, "bevor": 6.0, "avant": 7.0, "antes": 8.5,
    "ante": 6.0, "prima": 3.5, "davanti": 7.5, "devant": 4.5, "trước": 3.0, "قبل": 2.9,
}
# Nouns after which "of" has the "before" sense: "in front of", "ahead of", ...
AHEAD = {"front", "ahead", "advance", "eve"}
READY = {"ready", "prepared", "preparing", "preparation", "prepare", "preparations"}


def before_piece(prev, cur):
    """True if `cur` completes a before-word that started in the previous token(s)."""
    word = (prev + cur).strip().lower()
    piece = cur.strip().lower()
    return bool(piece) and any(
        word.endswith(w) and w.endswith(piece) and piece != w for w in BEFORE
    )


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the activation at the newest token from that token and the one before it.
    Stateless: no carry is needed."""
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    name = prev.strip().lower()
    key = tok.strip().lower()

    if tok == " of" and name == "anticipation":
        return None, 3.0
    if tok in (" front", " advance") and prev == " in":
        return None, 4.5
    if key == "to" and name == "prior":
        return None, 4.2
    if key == "for" and name in READY:
        return None, 2.8
    if key == "before" and name == "as":
        return None, 1.4
    if key in BEFORE and (tok.startswith(" ") or tok in ("before", "Before")):
        return None, BEFORE[key]
    if tok in ("vor", "voor"):
        return None, 3.0
    if before_piece(prev, tok) or (name == "v" and key.startswith("or")):
        return None, 8.0
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate the short boundary signal following a capitalized personal name.

A name is suggested by consecutive capitalized words, person senses in WordNet,
dictionary-unknown words, initials and honorifics. Descriptive words count less.
Word frequency helps distinguish names from common descriptive phrases. Short
parenthetical descriptions may separate a name from its continuation. The signal
appears on punctuation and grammatical continuations, not on the name itself.
Jr and Sr have separate suffix responses. Other token types get a small baseline.
The rolling text window resets at each document boundary.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
WORDS = re.compile(r'[^\W\d_]+')
TITLES = {'mr', 'mrs', 'ms', 'dr', 'prof', 'sir', 'madam', 'st', 'rev', 'fr'}
FUNCTION = set(('a an the of and for in on at by to from with as but or nor '
                'is was has had it this that these those i he she we they '
                'you his her my our its their').split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def properties(word):
    classes = wordnet.categories(word)
    return ('noun.person' in classes, not classes,
            'noun.location' in classes,
            bool(wordnet.parts_of_speech(word) - {'noun'}),
            zipf_frequency(word, 'en'))


def name_strength(text):
    words = list(WORDS.finditer(text))
    if not words:
        return 0.0, 30, False
    last = words[-1]
    word = last.group()
    trailing = text[last.end():]
    distance = len(trailing)
    if not word[0].isupper():
        return 0.0, distance, ',' in trailing
    chain = []
    next_start = last.end()
    for match in reversed(words):
        w = match.group()
        gap = text[match.end():next_start]
        if chain:
            if not gap or any(c not in " .-'’" for c in gap):
                break
            if '.' in gap and len(w) > 1 and w.lower() not in TITLES:
                break
        if not w[0].isupper() or w.lower() in FUNCTION:
            break
        chain.append(w)
        next_start = match.start()
    person, unknown, place, descriptive, frequency = properties(word)
    earlier_person = min(3, sum(properties(w)[0] for w in chain[1:]))
    earlier_unknown = min(3, sum(properties(w)[1] for w in chain[1:]))
    pure_people = min(3, sum(properties(w)[0] and not properties(w)[3]
                             for w in chain[1:]))
    common_unknown = min(3, sum(properties(w)[1] and 3.5 <= properties(w)[4] <= 5.3
                                for w in chain[1:]))
    initials = min(3, sum(len(w) == 1 for w in chain))
    honorific = any(w.lower() in TITLES for w in chain)
    # Coefficients are fitted on training name-boundary examples.
    score = (0.137 - 0.095 * (word.isupper() and len(word) > 1)
             + 0.197 * person + 0.145 * unknown + 0.031 * place
             - 0.066 * descriptive - 0.065 * max(frequency - 4, 0)
             - 0.046 * earlier_person + 0.151 * earlier_unknown
             + 0.323 * pure_people + 0.129 * common_unknown
             + 0.094 * initials + 0.194 * honorific
             + 0.159 * (len(chain) >= 2) - 0.064 * (len(chain) >= 3))
    return max(0.0, min(1.6, score)), distance, ',' in trailing


ASIDE = re.compile(r'\s*\([^()]{0,90}\)\s*(?:is|was)?$')
CONTINUATIONS = {' was': 0.71, ' is': 0.26, ' et': 1.74,
                 ' v': 1.1, ' vs': 0.2, ' of': 0.1}
ARTICLES = {' a', ' an', ' the'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    carry = (doc, (text + token)[-180:])
    if token == ' Jr':
        return carry, 1.76
    whitespace = token.isspace() and '\n' not in token and '\r' not in token
    comma = ',' in token and len(token) < 5
    paren = token.strip() in ('(', '（')
    if not (comma or paren or whitespace or token in ARTICLES
            or token in CONTINUATIONS or token == ' Sr'):
        return carry, -0.004

    strength, distance, after_comma = name_strength(text)
    aside = False
    match = ASIDE.search(text)
    before = text[:match.start()] if match else None
    if token.startswith(')') and '(' in text:
        before = text.rsplit('(', 1)[0]
    if before is not None:
        earlier, _, _ = name_strength(before.rstrip())
        if earlier > strength:
            strength, distance, aside = earlier, 0, True

    if token == ' Sr':
        value = 0.1 + 1.4 * min(1.0, strength)
    elif token == ',':
        value = 1.04 * strength if distance <= 1 else 0.04 + 0.5 * strength
    elif paren:
        value = 0.91 * strength if distance <= 1 else -0.02
    elif token in ARTICLES:
        scale = 1.39 if after_comma or aside else 0.4
        value = scale * strength if distance <= 2 else 0.0
    elif token in CONTINUATIONS:
        value = CONTINUATIONS[token] * strength if distance <= 1 else 0.0
    elif whitespace:
        if after_comma and distance <= 1:
            value = 0.11 + 1.34 * strength
        else:
            value = 0.06 * strength if after_comma else 0.0
    else:
        value = (0.245 if token == '.,' else 0.03) + 0.6 * strength
    return carry, float(value)

"""Name-list punctuation detector.

A layer-1 MLP component that is quiet on most text but fires on punctuation and short
connectives that come straight after proper names, and more so when the text around them
is name-dense: author lists, cast lists, bylines, citations, "Name, Jr.", "Name (born ...)",
"Name, a <role>". The strongest responses are on "Jr"/"Sr" and "., " after a name; a
comma or parenthesis after a name is a moderate response; ordinary words give ~0.

Prediction = trigger strength x name density, where name density is the share of the
previous 8 tokens (same document) that begin with a capital letter, capped at 4 names.
"""

READS = ()

NAME_WINDOW = 8   # how many previous tokens to look at
MAX_NAMES = 4     # density saturates at this many capitalized tokens

# how strongly each token drives the component when it follows a name-dense stretch
TRIGGER = {
    " Jr": 2.2,
    " Sr": 1.7,
    ".,": 0.8,
    " et": 0.6,
    " v": 0.5,
    ",": 0.3,
    "),": 0.3,
    " (": 0.2,
    " was": 0.1,
    " a": 0.1,
    " an": 0.1,
    " ": 0.1,
}


def starts_capitalized(token):
    return token.strip()[:1].isupper()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    current = tokens[-1]
    strength = TRIGGER.get(current, 0.0)
    if strength == 0.0:
        return carry, 0.0
    names = 0
    for j in range(len(tokens) - 2, max(-1, len(tokens) - 2 - NAME_WINDOW), -1):
        if docs[j] != docs[-1]:
            break
        if starts_capitalized(tokens[j]):
            names += 1
    return carry, strength * min(names, MAX_NAMES) / MAX_NAMES

"""Detect letters being introduced or referred to as mathematical names.

A letter (or Greek name) after a quantity or mathematical-object descriptor
gets a strong negative response. Naming words give a weaker response, and
connectives a still weaker one. Case and the common English words 'a' and
'I' modulate the strength. Letters within words or equations are mostly
quiet. State resets at document boundaries; split Greek bytes are joined
conceptually by carrying their response forward one token.
"""
import re
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
GREEK = set('''alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa
lambda mu nu xi omicron pi rho sigma tau upsilon phi chi psi omega'''.split())
QUANTITIES = set('''angle area current density depth diameter distance energy
force frequency height length magnitude mass momentum position power pressure
radius rate ratio resistance scale size speed temperature time velocity volume
wavelength weight width'''.split())
OBJECTS = set('''coefficient constant degree dimension eigenvalue exponent
factor field function graph group index integer interval line matrix node
number operation parameter plane point polynomial quantity rank region relation
ring scalar sensor set side space subset tensor term value variable vector
vertex'''.split())
INTRODUCERS = set('''let where wherein denote define choose take consider
assume give arbitrary fixed each any every all some pick find call name
determine'''.split())
LINKS = set('''and of for in to from with by at on is are be was were as that
when'''.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def descriptor(word):
    forms = set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) | {word}
    if forms & QUANTITIES:
        return 'quantity'
    if forms & OBJECTS:
        return 'object'
    if forms & INTRODUCERS:
        return 'introducer'
    return None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    same_doc = carry is not None and carry[0] == doc
    history, pending = (carry[1], carry[2]) if same_doc else ('', None)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    raw = prefix.token_bytes[-1].strip()
    name = token.strip().lstrip('$\\{-')
    latin = len(name) == 1 and name.isascii() and name.isalpha()
    greek_lead = raw in (b'\xce', b'\xcf')
    greek = name.lower() in GREEK or greek_lead or (
        len(name) == 1 and name.isalpha()
        and 'GREEK' in unicodedata.name(name, '')
    )
    value = 0.0
    # A split two-byte Greek letter gets the same signal on its final byte.
    if pending is not None and len(raw) == 1 and 128 <= raw[0] < 192:
        value = pending
    elif latin or greek:
        tail = history.rstrip(' \\${}\"\'“”‘’')
        match = re.search(r'([^\W\d_]+)\Z', tail)
        word = match.group(1).lower() if match else ''
        command = match and match.start() > 0 and tail[match.start()-1] == '\\'
        continued = token[0].isalnum() and history and history[-1].isalnum()
        english = name in ('a', 'I')
        capital = name.isupper()
        kind = descriptor(word) if len(word) > 1 and not command else None
        if continued:
            value = 0.0
        elif not history:
            value = -0.10
        elif kind == 'quantity':
            value = -0.10 if english else -0.40 if capital else -0.70
        elif kind == 'object':
            value = -0.40 if english else -0.50
        elif kind == 'introducer':
            value = -0.06 if english else -0.25
        elif word in LINKS:
            value = 0.0 if english else -0.06 if capital else -0.14
        elif tail and (tail[-1].isdigit() or tail[-1] in '=+-*/^_<>'):
            value = 0.025
        elif len(word) > 1 and not command:
            value = 0.0 if english else -0.025
        else:
            value = -0.03 if greek else -0.008
    pending = value if greek_lead else None
    return (doc, (history + token)[-120:], pending), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4705 -- a sparse 'math symbol in math prose' detector (negative).

What it does, in plain terms:
  * On a single-letter or Greek-letter math symbol (a, x, t, r, theta, ...), in running
    English text that is talking about mathematics or physics, the component pushes
    negative. The more science/maths words appear in the ~25 words before the symbol,
    the more negative (down to about -0.12).
  * On the first token of a document (right after <|endoftext|>), it is mildly negative.
  * Everywhere else it predicts 0.
"""
import unicodedata

MATH_WORDS = set("""let suppose consider denote define defined where function equation
variable variables matrix vector velocity speed length width angle time distance mass
radius probability integer prime polynomial limit derivative set sequence value
coefficient approaches positive negative real number solve find prove theorem if then
such that for all given is equal calculate formula rate force energy temperature weight
area volume integral sum constant parameter""".split())

READS = ()


def is_math_symbol(token):
    s = token.strip()
    if len(s) == 1 and s.isascii() and s.isalpha():
        return True
    if len(s) == 1 and "GREEK" in unicodedata.name(s, ""):
        return True
    return s in {"theta", "phi", "alpha", "beta", "tau", "gamma", "delta", "sigma", "lambda", "omega", "mu", "rho"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return None, -0.08  # first token of a document
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if not is_math_symbol(token):
        return None, 0.0
    words = [w.strip().lower() for w in prefix.token_strings[-26:-1]]
    score = sum(w in MATH_WORDS for w in words)
    return None, -0.02 * min(score, 6)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 4706: a "still" detector.

Its job is to write a strong "the word 'still' is here" signal into the
residual stream. It fires on the word still (" still", " Still", "still")
at about 5.3, and only weakly on a few other words that start "st" and look
like it (stiff, stuff, stir, stub, sty/styl, stationary, ...), at about 1.5.
Everything else is 0. Predicts activation from the current token alone.
"""

READS = ()

STILL_ACTIVATION = 5.3
ST_WORDS = {
    "stiff", "stuff", "stuffed", "stir", "stirring", "stub", "stunt",
    "stall", "stalled", "stationary", "sty", "styl", "stip", "stil",
}
ST_ACTIVATION = 1.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word == "still":
        value = STILL_ACTIVATION
    elif word in ST_WORDS:
        value = ST_ACTIVATION
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Closing quotation marks: the component fires on the quote that ends a quoted string,
most strongly when the string is a long code/JSON value that closes a tool call or
a list item; dot runs and the first token of a document are slightly negative."""
import re
READS = ()
DOT_RUN = re.compile(r"^·+$")
CLOSING = re.compile(r'["”»][,.;:)\]}]*\s*$')
JSON_END = ('"}}\n', '"]', '}",', ')",', '.",', '-",', '"}}')
def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    last = None if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry   # position of previous quote mark
    closes = '"' in s and CLOSING.search(s) is not None and not s.startswith(" ")
    if DOT_RUN.match(s.strip() or "x"):
        v = -0.33
    elif new_doc:
        v = -0.05
    elif s in JSON_END:
        v = 0.3
    elif closes and last is not None and t - last >= 20:
        v = 0.15
    elif closes and last is not None:
        v = 0.05
    else:
        v = 0.0
    return (t if '"' in s else last), float(v)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4709 -- the "on / since" component.

What it does: this MLP output direction fires when the model reads the Chinese
locative/temporal word 上 ("on, upon", as in 微博上, 沙发上的, 世界上) or the
temporal postposition 以来 / 年来 ("since, over the years", as in 2018年以来).
It is near zero on almost every other token.

The program does this with a small lookup of those words, each given the mean
activation observed for it in the training text. Everything else predicts 0,
which is the component's typical (near-zero) value.

Limits: these words account for only a few percent of the component's variance.
Most of its activation is small, spread across many tokens, with no clear
concept, and the first token of each document has large but unpredictable values.
"""

READS = ()

# mean activation seen for each word in training text
LOCATIVE = {
    "上": 0.63,      # bare 上 "on / upon"
    " 上": 0.6,
    "上的": 1.16,    # 上 + 的, as in 沙发上的
    "世界上": 0.66,
    "路上": 0.27,
    "以来": 1.0,     # "since", as in 2018年以来
    "年来": 1.25,    # "over the years", as in 这几年来
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token: the word's mean if it is a listed locative
    or temporal word, else 0."""
    return carry, LOCATIVE.get(prefix.token_strings[-1], 0.0)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 4710: a weak feature that is mostly quiet.

What it responds to, in plain terms (fitted on about 8k training rows):
1. The first token of a document. Its value depends on what kind of token it is:
   special markers like <|im_start|> lean positive; newlines, spaces, '#' and '"' lean
   negative; capitalised or lowercase words lean slightly negative; commas lean positive.
2. Broken-text fragments: a token that alone decodes to U+FFFD is a piece of a multi-byte
   UTF-8 character. It is mildly positive, more so when many fragments occur in the
   preceding 16 tokens (garbled or mojibake text).
3. The two-dot leader token '··' (repeated middle dots, as in a row of dot leaders): strongly
   negative, about -1.9 in the one run seen in the sample.
Everywhere else it predicts 0, which is close to its typical value.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

REPLACEMENT = "�"
DOT_LEADER = "··"
WINDOW = 16


def first_token_value(token):
    if token.startswith("<|"):
        return 0.4
    if token.strip() == "":
        return -0.4
    if token.lstrip(" ")[:1] in ('#', '"'):
        return -0.6
    if token.lstrip(" ")[:1] == ",":
        return 0.3
    if token[:1].isupper():
        return -0.15
    if token[:1].islower():
        return -0.08
    return -0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    token = prefix.token_strings[t]
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    recent = [] if carry is None or new_doc else list(carry)
    fragment = token == REPLACEMENT
    value = 0.0
    if new_doc:
        value = first_token_value(token)
    if fragment:
        value = 0.01 + 0.012 * min(sum(recent), 8)
    if token == DOT_LEADER:
        value = -1.9
    recent = (recent + [fragment])[-WINDOW:]
    return tuple(recent), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4711 -- a digit-"5" detector, with two weak extras.

What it does (activation = how much this one rank-one piece adds to the residual stream):

* The digit "5" is the main trigger, and how strongly it fires depends on what the
  "5" is glued to. A "5" stuck onto letters, as in a name or identifier
  (html5, md5, hdf5, PyQt5, x5), gives a strong positive value (about 0.7).
  A "5" after a space gives a small positive value, after a decimal point
  ("3.5", "$5.00") it is slightly negative, and in other places it is weakly positive.
* The second digit of day-of-month or year-like numbers after a "3" ("30", "31") is
  weakly positive, with "0" the stronger one.
* The first token of a document (where the model sees no earlier text) is
  negative on average (about -0.22). `DOC_START` sets it to -0.1: at -0.22 the rule
  raised variance explained but made next-token predictions clearly worse on eval;
  at -0.1 variance explained stays at 0.085 (0.094 at -0.22, 0.062 without the rule)
  and the cross-entropy cost is about half.

Everything else gives 0. Most of the component's variance is diffuse small activations
over ordinary text that no short rule captures.

Usage: `step(carry, prefix, upstream)` is called once per token; it reads only the
current token, the one before it, and the document labels, so it is causal.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation of a document's first token (it has no earlier context).
DOC_START = -0.1

# "5" by what precedes it.
FIVE_AFTER_LETTER = 0.66   # html5, md5, hdf5, x5: a digit glued onto a name
FIVE_AFTER_SPACE = 0.2     # " 5"
FIVE_AFTER_DOT = -0.2      # "3.5", "$5.00"
FIVE_OTHER = 0.1           # after a digit, a comma, a bracket, etc.

# Second digit of 30 / 31 and similar numbers after a "3".
AFTER_THREE = {"0": 0.4, "1": 0.18}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, DOC_START
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    last = before[-1:]
    if token == "5":
        if last.isascii() and last.isalpha():
            return None, FIVE_AFTER_LETTER
        if last == " ":
            return None, FIVE_AFTER_SPACE
        if last == ".":
            return None, FIVE_AFTER_DOT
        return None, FIVE_OTHER
    if before == "3" and token in AFTER_THREE:
        return None, AFTER_THREE[token]
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4712 -- a "sha / ha fragment" detector.

This component is almost silent on ordinary text. It fires (strongly, and with
causal importance near 1) on a few kinds of short sub-word pieces:

* Latin-script fragments of the letters "sha" or "ha" that sit inside a longer
  word or name: "sha" in SHA-1 / sha256 / pbkdf2:sha25, "SHA" in SHA-256,
  "_sha" in test names, "Sha" in Sharma-like names, "ha" in Deshа / Moeshа,
  and so on. Its activation is strongly negative there.
* Persian suffix pieces: the plural suffix "ها" and the bare "ا" in Persian
  text are strongly negative; the Persian ezafe-style "ای" written after "ه"
  (as in "ماهه‌ای", "عرضه‌ای") is strongly positive; " ا" (space + alef)
  in Persian is mildly positive.
* A run of middle dots "··" (text leaders) gives a small, very steady negative.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The values are rounded group means measured on
training text. The program is causal: it reads only the current token and the
text so far.
"""

READS = ()

# Letters that occur in Persian (Farsi) but not in standard Arabic.
PERSIAN_LETTERS = set("پچژگکی")

# The fragment "sha" by itself, with or without a leading space or underscore.
SHA_EXACT = {"sha", " sha", "SHA", " SHA", "_sha", ".sha"}
# Other pieces that end in "sha" or are mixed-case "Sha": weaker negative.
SHA_OTHER = {"Sha", " Sha", "pha", "isha", "asha", "acha", "tha", "aha", "Cha", "cha", " Shah"}
# The fragment "ha" (not "hash", not " ha", which is near 0).
HA_PIECES = {"ha", "HA"}

SHA_EXACT_VALUE = -9.0
SHA_OTHER_VALUE = -4.0
HA_VALUE = -3.0
DOTS_VALUE = -1.3
PERSIAN_HA_VALUE = -7.0  # plural suffix ها
PERSIAN_ALEF_VALUE = -4.0  # bare ا (no leading space)
PERSIAN_SPACE_ALEF_VALUE = 1.3  # " ا"
PERSIAN_AI_AFTER_HA = 7.7  # ای right after ه
OTHER_AI_VALUE = 0.3  # ای elsewhere


def _is_persian(text):
    """True when the last 40 characters hold at least two Persian-only letters."""
    return sum(ch in PERSIAN_LETTERS for ch in text[-40:]) >= 2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]
    persian = _is_persian(text)
    before = prefix.text_prefixes[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""

    if token in SHA_EXACT:
        return carry, SHA_EXACT_VALUE
    if token in SHA_OTHER:
        return carry, SHA_OTHER_VALUE
    if token in HA_PIECES:
        return carry, HA_VALUE
    if token == "··":
        return carry, DOTS_VALUE
    if token == "ای":
        return carry, PERSIAN_AI_AFTER_HA if persian and before.endswith("ه") else OTHER_AI_VALUE
    if persian:
        if token == "ها":
            return carry, PERSIAN_HA_VALUE
        if token == "ا":
            return carry, PERSIAN_ALEF_VALUE
        if token == " ا":
            return carry, PERSIAN_SPACE_ALEF_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4713 — a weak "start of a document" detector.

What it does: predicts a small positive activation (0.13) on the first token of each
document (the first token of a row, or the first token after a document boundary inside a
packed row), and 0 everywhere else.

Why: this is the only robust, readable pattern found. Over 24,678 document-start tokens in
training rows the activation averages +0.134 (std 0.36); everywhere else it averages about
0 with std 0.05 and no lexical, script or positional pattern that a short rule captures.
Large spikes do occur on replacement characters (U+FFFD, a fragment of a multi-byte
character), but their sign depends on which byte the fragment is, which a program that sees
only decoded text cannot read, so the program predicts their mean (about 0) there.

Limits: explains about 2% of the variance, and changes the model's output almost nothing
(its KL is about the same as switching the component off).
"""

READS = ()

DOCUMENT_START_ACTIVATION = 0.13


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return None, (DOCUMENT_START_ACTIVATION if starts_document else 0.0)

"""Approximate the component's negative response to school-subject labels.

Recognize subject names (including words split across tokens), then add
context shifts for headings, school grades, named exams, course labels,
and nearby educational words. Ordinary mentions have much smaller offsets.
Chinese school-year and textbook-volume markers have separate rules.
A short history resets at document boundaries; all other tokens get -0.001.
This models the subject-label pattern, not small background fluctuations.
"""
import re

READS = ()
GROUPS = {
    'math': ('math', 'mathematics', 'mathematical'),
    'math_fields': ('algebra', 'geometry', 'calculus', 'trigon', 'arithmetic',
                    'statistics', 'probability', 'quant', 'quantitative',
                    'mechanics', 'mensuration'),
    'science': ('science', 'sciences', 'scientific'),
    'natural_sciences': ('physics', 'physic', 'chemistry', 'biology', 'geology',
                         'astronomy', 'ecology', 'biochemistry', 'anatomy'),
    'english': ('english',),
    'languages': ('chinese', 'french', 'spanish', 'german', 'japanese',
                   'latin', 'russian', 'arabic'),
    'humanities': ('history', 'geography', 'philosophy', 'literature',
                    'grammar', 'linguistics'),
    'social_sciences': ('psychology', 'sociology', 'economics', 'logic',
                        'politics', 'studies', 'finance'),
    'arts': ('art', 'arts', 'music', 'drama'),
    'aptitude': ('aptitude', 'reasoning'),
    'computing': ('computer', 'computing', 'informatics'),
    'language_exams': ('ielts', 'toefl'),
    'chinese_language': ('语文',),
    'chinese_subjects': ('数学', '英语', '物理', '化学', '生物',
                         '地理', '历史', '政治', '美术', '音乐', '科学', '听力'),
}
ENGLISH_WORD = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z]+$')
SUBJECTS = {word: group for group, words in GROUPS.items() for word in words}
EDUCATION = re.compile(
    r'\b(?:school|college|university|grade|class|student|learn|learning|'
    r'teach|teaching|study|studying|exam|test|homework|course|lesson|'
    r'worksheet|curriculum|subject|subjects|tutor|pre|intro|advanced|ap|'
    r'education|educational|educated|primary|secondary|practice|questions)\b', re.I)
HEADING = re.compile(r'#{1,6}\s*[^#\n]{0,60}$')
LIST = re.compile(r'(?:^|\n)\s*(?:\d+[.)]\s*|[-*•]\s*)[^\n]{0,20}$')
GRADE = re.compile(r'\b(?:class|grade|year)\s*[-:]?\s*(?:\d{1,2}|[ivx]+)\b', re.I)
EXAM = re.compile(r'\b(?:gmat|ielts|toefl|cbse|icse|ncert|jee|neet|gcse|iift)\b', re.I)
CHINESE_GRADE = re.compile(
    r'[一二三四五六七八九十１２３４５６７８９0-9]年级'
)
WEIGHTS = {
    'math': -0.295,
    'math_fields': -0.139,
    'science': -0.337,
    'natural_sciences': -0.61,
    'english': 0.057,
    'languages': 0.137,
    'humanities': -0.043,
    'social_sciences': -0.015,
    'arts': -0.018,
    'aptitude': -0.191,
    'computing': 0.002,
    'language_exams': -1.975,
    'chinese_language': -3.115,
    'chinese_subjects': 0.039,
    'education': -0.276,
    'heading': -0.301,
    'list': -0.304,
    'line_start': -0.46,
    'lowercase': 0.177,
    'textbook_volume': -3.908,
    'school_year': -2.056,
    'numbered_grade': -2.229,
    'exam': -3.185,
    'chinese_grade': -3.115,
    'subject_label': -1.606,
    'course_level': -1.286,
    'heading_start': -1.645,
    'paragraph_start': -0.192,
}


def features(history, token):
    """Return a subject group plus a few ordinary context indicators."""
    if not token:
        return {}
    before = ENGLISH_WORD.search(history)
    old_word = (before.group().lower()
                if before and token and token[0].isascii() and token[0].isalpha()
                else '')
    joined = history + token
    word_match = ENGLISH_WORD.search(joined)
    word = word_match.group().lower() if word_match else ''
    group = None
    # The root is enough for mathematical compounds such as Mathematica.
    if word.startswith('math') and not old_word.startswith('math'):
        group = 'math'
    elif word.startswith('trigon') and not old_word.startswith('trigon'):
        group = 'math_fields'
    elif word in SUBJECTS and word != old_word:
        group = SUBJECTS[word]
    for subject in GROUPS['chinese_subjects'] + GROUPS['chinese_language']:
        if joined.endswith(subject) and not history.endswith(subject):
            group = SUBJECTS[subject]
            break
    if group is None:
        if token in ('上', '下') and (
            CHINESE_GRADE.search(history[-12:]) or
            history.endswith(tuple(GROUPS['chinese_subjects'] + GROUPS['chinese_language']))
        ):
            return {'textbook_volume': 1.0}
        if token == '级' and re.search(r'[一二三四五六七八九十0-9]年$', history):
            return {'school_year': 1.0}
        return {}
    context = history[:-len(old_word)] if old_word else history
    f = {group: 1.0}
    if re.search(r'(?:course|subjects?|topics?|category)\s*[:,/]?\s*$', context, re.I):
        f['subject_label'] = 1.0
    if re.search(r'\b(?:pre|introductory|general|college|ap|advanced)\s*$', context, re.I):
        f['course_level'] = 1.0
    if GRADE.search(context[-80:]):
        f['numbered_grade'] = 1.0
    if EXAM.search(context[-100:]):
        f['exam'] = 1.0
    if CHINESE_GRADE.search(context[-30:]):
        f['chinese_grade'] = 1.0
    if EDUCATION.search(context[-100:]):
        f['education'] = 1.0
    if re.search(r'#{1,6}\s*$', context):
        f['heading_start'] = 1.0
    if re.search(r'\n\s*\n\s*$', context):
        f['paragraph_start'] = 1.0
    if HEADING.search(context):
        f['heading'] = 1.0
    if LIST.search(context):
        f['list'] = 1.0
    if not context.strip() or context.endswith('\n'):
        f['line_start'] = 1.0
    if word_match and word_match.group().islower():
        f['lowercase'] = 1.0
    return f


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    past = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else b''
    history = past.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    joined = past + prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    text = joined.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    token = text[len(history):]
    f = features(history, token)
    value = -0.001 + sum(WEIGHTS.get(k, 0.0)*v for k,v in f.items())
    return (doc, joined[-180:]), float(value)
